# LG THERMA V + Shelly Pro EM-50 / Shelly Pro Modbus Add-on

> Tested community integration for local RS-485 / Modbus RTU monitoring and limited control of a compatible LG THERMA V heat pump using Shelly Pro EM-50, Shelly Pro Modbus Add-on, Shelly Virtual Components and optional Home Assistant exposure.

## Canonical project

- Repository: https://github.com/drHouse-gif/lg-therma-v-shelly
- Human documentation: `README.md`
- Machine-oriented context: `docs/AI_CONTEXT.md`
- Structured metadata: `project.yaml`
- Virtual Component installer: `scripts/01-create-virtual-components.js`
- Runtime Modbus bridge: `scripts/02-lg-therma-v-modbus-bridge.js`
- Upstream submission notes: `docs/UPSTREAM_SUBMISSION.md`

## Hardware requirements

- Target HVAC device: compatible LG THERMA V heat pump with documented Modbus RTU access.
- Shelly controller: Shelly Pro EM-50.
- RS-485 interface: Shelly Pro Modbus Add-on / compatible supported RS-485 Add-on.
- Physical bus: shielded twisted pair for RS-485 A/B; installation and termination must follow the actual bus topology and equipment documentation.
- Optional current transformers on Shelly Pro EM-50 for electrical energy measurement.

## Tested Modbus RTU parameters

- Physical layer: RS-485.
- Protocol: Modbus RTU.
- Baud rate: 9600.
- Frame: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (`8N1`).
- Tested LG slave/server ID: `2`.
- Shelly Serial component ID: `100`.
- Shelly `MbRtuClient` component ID: `100`.
- Shelly RPC register addresses in this project are zero-based.
- Normal background state refresh: every 10 seconds.

## Data/register map used by this project

| Semantic value | Modbus area | Zero-based address | Direction | Encoding | Shelly VC |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Main power | Coil | 0 | R/W | Boolean | `boolean:200` |
| DHW enable | Coil | 1 | R/W | Boolean | `boolean:201` |
| Silent mode | Coil | 2 | R/W | Boolean | `boolean:202` |
| Heating-water target | Holding register | 2 | R/W | signed 16-bit ×0.1 °C | `number:203` |
| DHW target | Holding register | 8 | R/W | signed 16-bit ×0.1 °C | `number:204` |
| Inlet-water temperature | Input register | 2 | Read | signed 16-bit ×0.1 °C | `number:205` |
| Outlet-water temperature | Input register | 3 | Read | signed 16-bit ×0.1 °C | `number:206` |
| DHW temperature | Input register | 5 | Read | signed 16-bit ×0.1 °C | `number:207` |
| Error code | Input register | 0 | Read | unsigned 16-bit | `number:209` |

Exactly nine Virtual Components are used. `number:208` is intentionally unused.

## Runtime logic

1. Verify the required nine Virtual Components.
2. Verify/configure the Shelly Serial/Modbus client component.
3. Read real LG state before enabling writes.
4. Publish the physical state into Shelly Virtual Components.
5. Enable control handlers only after successful initial synchronization.
6. Send writes only for supported controls.
7. Read the changed value back after a write so the UI reflects physical state.
8. Refresh the complete state every 10 seconds.

The first-read-before-write behavior is a deliberate safety mechanism to prevent stale Shelly UI defaults from being pushed into the heat pump after restart.

## Home Assistant

Home Assistant is optional. The Modbus logic runs locally on Shelly. Supported Virtual Components can be exposed through the standard Home Assistant Shelly integration. This project does not create a native Home Assistant `climate` entity by itself.

## Safety and scope

- Community project; not an official LG, Shelly Group or Home Assistant integration.
- LG THERMA V generations, controller boards, connectors, Modbus enablement procedures, slave IDs, register maps and safe limits can differ by exact model.
- On the tested installation the communications connector was associated with `CN_COM`; this must not be generalized to every THERMA V model.
- Verify the exact service documentation before writing values.
- Never write undocumented registers and never use this integration to bypass LG safety logic.
- HVAC electrical compartments may contain dangerous mains voltage; follow manufacturer isolation and service procedures.
- Current upstream-readiness limitation: `ALLTERCO/shelly-script-examples` expects runtime scripts using Virtual Components to be self-contained, while this project currently provisions its fixed VCs with a separate one-time installer.
